newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senators appeal to Albright over Vanunu.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators appeal to Albright over Vanunu.

text.p: Two U.S. senators have called on Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to press Israel on the case of Mordechai Vanunu, the nuclear technician jailed for disclosing details of Israel's nuclear programme.

Democratic senators Russell Feingold of Wisconsin and Paul Wellstone of Minnesota said they were raising the case because of reports of a deterioration in the mental health of Vanunu, who has been in solitary confinement for more than 10 years.

The case "appears to be one that ought to be reviewed on humanitarian grounds", they said in a letter to Albright dated March 3 and distributed Friday by the Wisconsin-based U.S. Campaign to Free Mordechai Vanunu.

"We would appreciate it if the State Department would be willing to look into this specific issue relating to Mr Vanunu's mental health and raise this case, on those grounds, with the Israeli government," the senators said.
Feingold and Wellstone said they were not suggesting that Vanunu, who was convicted of espionage and treason in 1986 and sentenced to 18 years, was not guilty of those acts.

Vanunu worked at Israel's Dimona nuclear complex before leaving the country in 1985 and telling London's Sunday Times newspaper that Israel had become a major nuclear weapons power with material for up to 200 nuclear warheads.
He was lured by an Israeli woman agent from London to Italy where he was kidnapped by Israeli agents, drugged and spirited back to the Jewish state.
Anti-nuclear and human rights groups in several countries have been appealing for years on Vanunu's behalf, but Israeli leaders have refused to show clemency.
Israel has never confirmed that it has nuclear weapons.
